## ✨ Highlights

- 🌐 **A network change no longer takes a VRRP node's virtual IP away**: applying a network configuration on the node holding a virtual IP removed keepalived's address - for a moment, until keepalived took it back. A node now removes only the addresses it put there itself ([network configuration](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/network-configuration.md)).
- 🛰️ **The same IPv6 anycast address on several nodes**: a `/128` - the address nodes announce with BGP - is added without duplicate address detection; every node but the first used to mark it a duplicate and leave it unused ([BGP](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/bgp.md)).
- 🔀 **Active/active behind a MikroTik router**: how RouterOS 7.22+ spreads the traffic over every node with BGP multipath, measured in the lab ([BGP multipath](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/bgp.md#activeactive-behind-routeros-bgp-multipath)).

## 🌐 Network

- **Other daemons' addresses stay** ([#342](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/342)): applying a network configuration added the addresses it lists and removed every other global address of the interface - keepalived's [VRRP](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/vrrp.md) virtual IPs included. On a cluster's master, keepalived saw its address go, left MASTER and took it back within the second: nothing measured lost, but a real cut each time the node's network changed. A node now marks the addresses it adds (the kernel's address protocol) and removes only those, and the address the kernel's DHCP obtained at boot once its interface leaves DHCP mode. It knows them after a janusd restart too.
- **An anycast `/128` on every node that announces it**: Linux checks that a new IPv6 address isn't already in use on the link (duplicate address detection), and the same anycast address on two nodes of one segment left the second "dadfailed" - present, never used. A single IPv6 address is now added without that check, as keepalived does for its virtual IPs; a `/64` keeps it.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **A refused HAProxy configuration is answered like the other refusals** ([#339](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/339)): through the Controller's API, a node refusing `ApplyConfig` - a cluster's lock, an invalid configuration - answered 502 with gRPC's words, as if the node were out of reach; it's now the node's message with 400 (403 for a role, 502 only for a node out of reach), as for files and certificates.

## 📖 Docs

- [BGP](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/bgp.md#activeactive-behind-routeros-bgp-multipath) ([#341](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/341)): active/active behind RouterOS 7.22+ - the router's configuration, `multipath` as a number (**0 leaves the anycast address unreachable**), BFD, the flows spread by addresses or by ports and FastTrack, what a route change does to open connections, measured against a single path.
- [VRRP](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/vrrp.md) ([#332](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/332)): an IPv6 virtual IP moved with the IPv4 instance (`virtual_ipaddress_excluded`), proven; network configuration, VRRP and BGP: which addresses a network change touches.
- [v2026.10.26's lab campaign](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.26.md) ([#340](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/340)).

## 🧪 Tests

- `qemu-vrrp-ipv6-test` (new, three enforcing nodes with a production cluster's keepalived configuration): an IPv6 virtual IP with the IPv4 one, the neighbours following a failover unasked; a network change on the master leaves its virtual IPs, and the same anycast `/32` and `/128` on two nodes both serve.
- netmgr's network-namespace test: another daemon's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses stay through changes, a `/128` a neighbour already holds comes up usable, the boot lease's address goes once out of DHCP mode.
